# ​​​​​​​Pre-Prosthetic Surgery


The preparation of your mouth before the placement of a denture (or prosthesis) is referred to as pre-prosthetic surgery. Some patients require minor oral surgical procedures before receiving a partial or complete denture, in order to ensure the maximum level of comfort and stability.

Since a dental prosthetic sits atop the bone ridge, that surface needs to be smooth. It must be of the proper shape and size. Pre-prosthetic surgery can be employed to mold the bone into the proper shape. Such procedures can include:

Torus/Tori removal

Tuberosity reduction

Alveoplasty

Removal of excess gum tissue

Pre-prosthetic surgery procedures are accomplished in complete comfort at our office. Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi will discuss surgical and anesthetic options with you during your consultation appointment.

When teeth are missing, the bone and soft tissue beneath the gums do not stay the same. Over time, the bony ridge that supports a denture or partial can become uneven, sharp, or irregular, making it difficult to achieve a secure, pain-free fit. If you are preparing to receive a partial or complete denture and the shape of your jaw requires adjustments first, pre-prosthetic surgery may be the right step to take before your prosthesis is placed.

At Wilshire Oral Surgery and Implant Center, our team brings board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgical training to every procedure we perform. Dr. Jonathan R. Shadi and Dr. Saman Vahedi each completed their training at the University of Southern California and hold advanced credentials in oral and maxillofacial surgery. Together, they will evaluate your jaw anatomy, review your restorative goals with your general dentist, and recommend only the procedures necessary to set you up for the best possible prosthetic outcome.


## What Pre-Prosthetic Surgery Involves


Pre-prosthetic surgery is the name for a group of oral surgical procedures performed before a denture or other removable prosthesis is fitted. Because a prosthesis rests directly on the gum ridge and underlying bone, any irregularities in that foundation can lead to sores, loosening, and chronic discomfort. The goal is to reshape or smooth the tissues so that the finished prosthesis sits evenly, stays in place, and causes no pain during everyday use.

According to published research in oral and maxillofacial surgery, proper pre-prosthetic preparation of the bony ridge is directly associated with improved prosthetic retention and stability for patients receiving dentures. You can read more about the evidence behind these procedures at the National Library of Medicine.


## Pre-Prosthetic Procedures We Perform


Depending on your anatomy and your restorative plan, one or more of the following procedures may be recommended. Our surgeons will explain what is needed and why during your consultation.

Alveoloplasty

The most common pre-prosthetic procedure. The alveolar ridge is contoured so that it is smooth, even, and shaped to support a denture.

Torus and Tori Removal

Bony outgrowths on the roof of the mouth or along the inner lower jaw can prevent a denture from seating properly.

Tuberosity Reduction

Reducing an enlarged tuberosity at the back of the upper jaw creates the clearance needed for a stable, well-fitting prosthesis.

Excess Gum Tissue Removal

Soft, flabby gum tissue is carefully contoured so the ridge beneath is firm and stable for denture support.

Ridge Reduction

Bone that is too prominent or sharp is reduced to provide a flat, comfortable base for a denture to rest against.

Bone or Tissue Grafting

If the ridge has resorbed significantly, grafting can rebuild volume. Learn more on our Bone Grafting page.

Not every patient requires all of these procedures. Our surgeons will perform a thorough examination to determine exactly what your situation calls for.


## Benefits of a Well-Prepared Jaw


Taking the time to prepare the supporting tissues before a prosthesis is placed can have a meaningful impact on your long-term comfort and confidence. Common benefits include less movement and slipping during eating and speaking, fewer pressure sores from an uneven bone surface, a more natural bite, and greater confidence when smiling or speaking in public.

## Sedation and Anesthesia Options


Pre-prosthetic procedures are accomplished with your comfort as the first priority. Local anesthesia is used routinely for minor soft tissue and bone contouring. For patients who prefer a more relaxed experience, IV sedation or general anesthesia is available in our office. You will have a full discussion about your options at your consultation.


## What to Expect at Your Consultation and Beyond


Your first step is a consultation with one of our oral surgeons. We will review your dental records, take any necessary imaging, and discuss what you are hoping to achieve. If pre-prosthetic surgery is recommended, we will coordinate with your general dentist or prosthodontist so that everyone involved in your care is aligned on timing and sequencing.

Most pre-prosthetic procedures are minor and carry a straightforward recovery. You will receive detailed post-operative instructions before you leave our office, and our team is available to answer any questions that come up during healing.

Consultation

We review your dental records, take imaging, and evaluate your jaw to determine which procedures are needed.

Treatment Day

The procedure is performed with your chosen anesthesia option. Most pre-prosthetic surgeries are completed in a single visit.

Healing

Tissues heal over one to several weeks depending on the procedure. Our team monitors your progress and supports your recovery.

Denture Placement

Once your surgeon confirms the ridge is ready, your restorative dentist proceeds with fitting your partial or complete denture.


## Schedule Your Pre-Prosthetic Surgery Consultation in Los Angeles


Dr. Shadi and Dr. Vahedi have the surgical training and the Los Angeles roots to guide you through every step of preparing for your prosthesis. Whether you need minor bone contouring or a more involved procedure, our team will give you the information you need to move forward with confidence.

To get started, request an appointment online or call our office at (310) 846-8978. We look forward to helping you build the foundation for a comfortable, stable smile.

mainEntity.name: Who needs pre-prosthetic surgery before getting dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every patient who receives dentures will need pre-prosthetic surgery first. Patients who are most likely to benefit include those who have been missing teeth for a long period of time (which allows bone resorption and ridge irregularities to develop), those with bony prominences such as tori, those with excess or flabby gum tissue, and those whose existing bone height or shape is not adequate to support a stable prosthesis. A consultation with one of our oral surgeons is the best way to determine whether surgery is needed in your specific case.

mainEntity.name: What is alveoloplasty and why is it performed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alveoloplasty is the reshaping and smoothing of the alveolar bone — the ridge of bone that holds the teeth. After teeth are extracted, the remaining bone can be sharp, uneven, or poorly contoured. Alveoloplasty removes these irregularities so that a denture can rest comfortably on a smooth, even surface. It is often performed at the same time as tooth extraction when a patient is transitioning to a complete or partial denture.

mainEntity.name: How long does recovery take after pre-prosthetic surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Recovery depends on the type and scope of the procedure. Minor tissue contouring and bone smoothing typically heal within one to two weeks. More involved procedures such as bone grafting or significant ridge reduction may require a longer healing period before denture placement can proceed. Our surgeons will give you a realistic recovery timeline at your consultation and provide detailed post-operative instructions to support a smooth healing process.

mainEntity.name: Can pre-prosthetic surgery be done at the same time as tooth extraction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In many cases, alveoloplasty or other minor bone-contouring procedures are performed at the same appointment as tooth extraction, particularly when the patient is planning to receive an immediate denture. Combining the procedures into one visit reduces overall treatment time and allows healing to begin for both the extraction sites and the reshaped ridge simultaneously. Your surgeon will review whether same-day preparation is appropriate for your treatment plan.

mainEntity.name: Does pre-prosthetic surgery affect my ability to receive dental implants later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pre-prosthetic surgery that involves bone grafting or ridge augmentation can actually improve your candidacy for dental implants down the road by maintaining or rebuilding bone volume. Procedures that reduce excess bone do not necessarily prevent future implant placement, but the specifics depend on your anatomy and how much bone remains. If you are considering implants as a long-term option, let your surgeon know during your consultation so the treatment plan can account for both your immediate prosthetic needs and your future goals.

mainEntity.name: Will pre-prosthetic surgery be covered by my insurance or financing plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coverage for pre-prosthetic procedures varies by insurance plan. Many plans provide partial coverage for procedures that are deemed medically necessary to support denture placement. Our team will review your benefits and provide a clear picture of your out-of-pocket costs before any procedure is scheduled. We also offer financing options for patients who need assistance managing costs.
